title: Harvest Knowledge hosted API search + rerank intro
summary: Introductory hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking for Harvest Knowledge's knowledge search use case. Covered API endpoints, rerank patterns, tradeoffs (latency vs cost), Redwood Console observability, security/compliance questions, and a proposed 10k-doc POC. Agreed next steps: security docs + pricing, run benchmark on 10k subset, schedule POC kickoff.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, with Carlos our SE. Quick intros?
[00:08] Lena (Harvest): Hi, Lena here - I run search at Harvest, we have Tom and Priya as well.
[00:13] Tom (Harvest): Tom, backend.
[00:15] Priya (Harvest CTO): Priya, CTO.
[00:18] Carlos (Redwood SE): Hey all, I'll lead the demo portion - we've got about 40ish minutes, so we'll walk through embeddings, the candidate retrieval pattern and the reranker, and then show Console traces and cost SLOs.
[00:30] Maya: Quick note - feel free to interrupt, we'll also capture action items.
[00:34] Evan (Product): Quick Q up front - we have a 50k doc KB, most queries are short, but we need good MRR. Target P95 latency under 150ms if possible.
[00:44] Carlos: Okay noted, that's helpful. For hosted API we typically do a two-step flow: 1) embeddings for query -> nearest neighbor retrieval from your vector store, 2) call /v1/rerank or a scoring model to rescore top-k candidates. We'll demo both.
[00:58] [01:00] Carlos: Starting slide - architecture. The embeddings endpoint returns 1k-d vectors in our example but you can choose model variants. Important: similarity metric, cosine vs dot, we recommend cosine for normalized embeddings.
[01:18] Lena: How do you handle batched queries? We have spikes from our UI.
[01:22] Carlos: Good Q. Hosted API supports request-level batching and our runtime does continuous batching on the GPU. In Console you can see batching profiles under Optimize where we suggest batch sizes based on your QPS to hit cost/latency targets.
[01:36] [02:05] Maya: Security quick note - we are SOC 2 compliant, SSO via SAML/Okta, and we can integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping. If you need on-prem or VPC private, that's a separate Private deployment option.
[02:18] Priya: We need audit logs and a KMS integration; can you send docs?
[02:22] Maya: Yes, we'll share the security or compliance package link after the call.
[02:27] [03:10] Carlos: Demo time. I'm going to switch to the console. First, embed a query via POST /v1/embeddings with model "redwood-sim-1" in the example. Response includes embedding vector and request id. Then we do an ANN lookup in your vector DB, we show top 100 candidate ids, then we call the rerank endpoint which accepts either embeddings for the candidates or the raw text and does a cross-encoder style rerank.
[03:40] Tom: Do you pass the full candidate text to rerank or embeddings?
[03:45] Carlos: Both are supported. Sending raw text to rerank (cross-encoder) gives better quality but higher compute per request. Sending candidate embeddings is cheaper and lower latency because reranker can do a fast dot-product scoring. For many setups we do hybrid: embedding recall for top-100 then cross-encoder rerank top-5.
[04:02] [04:50] Carlos: I'm calling rerank now with a small sample query; you can see trace lines: token time, kernel time, kv cache warmup. The Console trace shows p50/p95 latency and token-level cost.
[05:10] Lena: That trace view is nice. Can we tie traces to our request IDs?
[05:14] Carlos: Yes, you can pass an app-level request id in X-Request-ID and Console will link it to the trace.
[05:19] [06:00] Maya: On billing - hosted usage-based pricing: embeddings per vector and rerank per request (token/time). We'll include a pricing sample for your 50k DB and expected QPS.
[06:12] Priya: Also need data retention and opt-out - do you store queries?
[06:17] Maya: Default ephemeral logs for hosted, but enterprise accounts can opt-in for longer retention for diagnostics. We also support log export with redaction. KMS can be used to encrypt customer data at rest.
[06:32] [07:10] Tom: For performance, any suggestions on model selection? We care about both latency and quality.
[07:15] Carlos: If latency is priority, smaller sim models + embedding index (HNSW) with quantization in the vector store can help. For quality you choose a larger reranker cross-encoder. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization levels (8-bit, 4-bit) and batch sizes to hit business SLOs.
[07:38] [08:00] Carlos: Also prefix/KV caching matters for chat-style rerankers. For pure search it's less relevant but if you have sessions it's useful.
[08:12] [09:00] Carlos: I'm switching to a quick micro-benchmark we ran on a 10k doc subset: baseline recall@10 78%, rerank improved MRR by ~14% at p95 latency ~120ms using our hosted reranker with a top-20 candidate set.
[09:22] Lena: Can you share that benchmark data and the dataset schema?
[09:25] Carlos: Yes, we'll include the benchmark sheet and the test harness.
[09:30] [10:10] Evan: What's the recommended top-k to send to rerank? Top-20? top-100?
[10:14] Carlos: Tradeoff: top-100 gives higher ceiling but more compute. Practically many customers do top-20 to top-50, then cross-encoder top-5. For your 50k corpus top-20 is a good starting point.
[10:30] [11:00] Tom: Any built-in dedup or near-duplicate handling in rerank? We have lots of similar docs.
[11:06] Carlos: There's a dedupe post-processing step you can run client-side; we also support a server-side rerank param that penalizes near-duplicate scores via an overlap penalty heuristic. We'll document the parameter.
[11:20] [12:00] Maya: Quick check - who are your internal stakeholders? Priya: CTO, Lena: search, Tom: infra; Evan product. Good.
[12:12] [12:45] Carlos: Now on cost controls: you can pin routes to cheaper models or have fallback policies. Redwood routing will send queries to a cheaper sim model if you exceed dedicated capacity, for instance. You can set quality thresholds to prevent regressions.
[12:58] Lena: How do rollouts look? We need A/B.
[13:02] Carlos: Console supports canary and A/B with traffic splits by route/model. You can also compare metrics like MRR and latency per model in the metrics dashboard.
[13:20] [14:00] Priya: For compliance we need SOC2 report, ISO mention, and a data processing addendum (DPA).
[14:07] Maya: We'll attach SOC2 and DPA links.
[14:12] [14:50] Carlos: Demoing API request examples now - here's a sample body for rerank: {"query": "...", "candidates": [{"id": "123", "text":"..."}, ...]} and response gives scores and explanations. Note: explanation can be noisy due to model tokenization.
[15:20] Tom: Do you provide local scoring snippets for us to run as a fallback if Redwood is down?
[15:25] Carlos: For enterprise we can provide a private deployment package but not the model weights. You can also cache top answers in-memory as an application fallback.
[15:40] [16:30] Evan: What's the onboarding for a POC? How long?
[16:35] Maya: Typical POC 3-6 weeks: initial setup, ingest a 10k sample corpus, run benchmarks, tune reranker thresholds, then expand to full corpus.
[16:48] [17:10] Carlos: We'll run the benchmark harness against your 10k slice and return MRR/latency/cost estimates.
[17:20] [18:00] Maya: Okay I'm going to summarize next steps after the technical bits. Carlos anything else?
[18:05] Carlos: Quick notes on integration - SDKs in Python/Node, example code in our repo. Also note that embedding dimensionality differences mean you might need to reindex if switching models.
[18:25] Lena: Ouch, reindexing cost is a concern.
[18:27] Carlos: We can help with migration strategies: aliasing and shadow indexing to avoid downtime.
[18:40] [19:00] Priya: Any competitor differences we should be aware of?
[19:05] Maya: Many vendors offer embeddings + rerank; differences are in runtime efficiency, pricing transparency, and production features like rollback and routing. We'll include a short competitor matrix.
[19:18] Evan: Is there a limit to candidate text length for rerank?
[19:21] Carlos: For cross-encoder rerankers, token limits apply (we'll share model limits). We truncate with a smart heuristic that prefers beginning + salient sections.
[19:38] [20:00] Carlos: Live Q/A - Tom asks about KV cache again. For generative rerankers or chat, KV cache reduces repeated token compute; for pure search rerank it's minimal impact.
[20:20] Tom: Got it.
[20:25] [21:00] Maya: Ok wrapping - recap: we'll send security docs, pricing sample for 50k corpus, benchmark harness + results on 10k subset, and proposed POC plan.
[21:12] Lena: Sounds good.
[21:16] Priya: Timeline - can we get the security docs by Friday?
[21:19] Maya: Yes, we'll send by 2025-03-07.
[21:24] [22:00] Carlos: I'll include the benchmark spreadsheet and sample curl commands.
[22:10] Evan: Also include sample rerank params and suggested top-k.
[22:15] [23:00] Maya: Any final Qs?
[23:05] Lena: No, thank you.
[23:08] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts and a POC kickoff calendar invite.
[23:18] [End of recording]
